Baskerville42/outage-data-ua.body:
# outage-data-ua

A public repository and tools for automatically collecting, parsing, visualizing (HTML), and generating PNG images of charts of scheduled and emergency power outages in Ukraine.

The project retrieves data from open web pages of power providers and stores it as JSON "as is" in the `data/` directory. This data is then rendered in a fixed HTML template and converted into PNG images, which are saved to `images/<region>/gpv-x-x.png`.

---

## Data format
Each region is stored in a file `data/<region>.json`. Basic structure (abbreviated):

```json
{
  "regionId": "kyiv",
  "regionAffiliation": "м. Київ",
  "lastUpdated": "2025-11-06T11:41:56.430Z",
  "fact": { "updateFact": "06.11.2025 09:09" },
  "preset": { "updateFact": "04.11.2025 18:00" },
  "lastUpdateStatus": { "status": "parsed", "ok": true, "code": 200, "message": null, "at": "2025-11-06T11:41:56.430Z", "attempt": 5 },
  "meta": { "schemaVersion": "1.0.0", "contentHash": "..." }
}
```

- `preset` — scheduled outages for the week for each group (weekly template). Stored "as is", without structural normalization.

ChisaAlter/ChisaBot.description: ChisaBot: a self-hosted Chinese BOT platform supporting configurable models and Magpie integration
ChisaAlter/ChisaBot.body:
ChisaBot is developed from the open-source code of [CopilotKit/OpenBot](https://github.com/CopilotKit/OpenBot). It keeps AG-UI, multi-BOT, tool permissions, and audit capabilities, and adds a Chinese interface, standalone web login, local session persistence, the Magpie model catalog, and per-BOT model selection. This branch can store sessions in your own PostgreSQL by setting `OPENBOT_RUNTIME_MODE=local`, without a CopilotKit Intelligence project. Models are connected by administrators and can be self-hosted models, compatible APIs, or a self-deployed [Magpie](https://github.com/yetone/magpie) gateway. When you use third-party models, inference is still handled by the selected model service.

## Screenshots

> The following screenshots come from a fresh demo instance (demo account, demo bot, no real conversations).

### Web (server)

Light theme: the bot list is on the left, the conversation is in the middle, and the panel the bot created is in the right column.

### PC client (Windows)

ChisaBot PC is a borderless window. After opening, it goes directly to the ChisaBot on your server, and the window buttons are in the top right. On first run, enter the server address on the local "Sign in to ChisaBot" page.

### Phone

The conversation and panel in a phone browser (390×844), and the sign-in page of the Android client.

## Existing features

- **Chinese interface**: chat, BOT management, settings, and admin pages are localized into Chinese. The built-in Chinese tenant pack is at `examples/zh-CN/`.
- **Web login**: login page, server-side sessions, and logout. The authentication gateway protects pages and APIs.
- **Local runtime and persistence**: local runtime mode uses PostgreSQL to store conversations, so you can still view sessions after a restart.
- **Model configuration**: administrators configure the protocol, API address, keys, and default deployment models, and can test the connection. Keys are encrypted and stored on the server.
- **Magpie model catalog**: reads the full list of models the gateway actually exposes, keeps provider prefixes, and supports search and refresh.
- **Per-BOT model selection**: the chat input and the BOT settings change the same persisted value. They stay in sync with each other and across browser tabs, and the next turn uses the new model.
- **Tools and permissions**: inherits upstream AG-UI integration, BOT computer, MCP tools, approvals, and audit. Each is enabled through deployment configuration.
- **Panels and cloud browser**: bots can create panels in the right column (optionally refreshed on a schedule), and can open and operate web pages in a cloud browser on the server. Switch between "Panels | Computer" in the right column to view them.
- **Clients and online updates**: the Windows PC (Electron) and Android clients connect to your own server. The server updates with one click at "Admin Console → System Update", and the web app and clients each prompt you when a new version is available.

Daninelli/opensource-market.body:
# 开源集市 (Open Source Market)

A navigation site for ready-to-use open-source applications, organized by category, for learning, development, and exchange.

- Plain HTML + CSS + vanilla JS, no framework, no build step
- All data lives in `projects.json`. Adding a project only requires editing this one file
- Can be deployed directly to GitHub Pages / Vercel / Netlify / any static server

Live site: <https://daninelli.github.io/opensource-market/>

## Submitting a New Project

No Git knowledge needed, and no files need to be edited.

Open [New issue](https://github.com/Daninelli/opensource-market/issues/new?template=submit.yml), choose the form 「**收录开源项目** (Submit Open-Source Project)」, and fill in four fields: project name, repository URL, top-level category, and a one-sentence description.

After submission, the Action automatically fetches the star count, last update time, license, latest Release, and installation packages from GitHub. Once validation passes, it creates a PR to add the project, which a maintainer reviews and merges. For the detailed process, see [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/Daninelli/opensource-market/blob/HEAD/CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Quick Start

For local preview, **do not double-click `index.html` directly**. For security reasons, browsers block `file://` pages from using `fetch` to read JSON in the same directory, and you will see the message 「数据没有加载出来」 ("data failed to load"). Instead, open it with any static server:

```bash
npx serve .          # or
python -m http.server 8000
```

Then visit `http://localhost:8000`.

## Directory Structure

├── index.html              # page structure + SVG icon sprite (all hand-drawn, no emoji)
├── app.js                  # category system, section rendering, filtering, search, popularity ranking

├── assets/recent.js        # script for the recently added page
├── projects.json           # project data (the site's only data source)

# Power Communication Message Parsing Tool

**Turns power communication messages from an unreadable string of hexadecimal into a table that explains each field clearly.**

A one-stop desktop tool for field debugging, integration testing, protocol development, and compliance verification in power communications. **Windows portable version**: single-file exe. Double-click to run. The target machine does not need Python or an internet connection.

3. **View the results** → parsing results are listed as layer → field → raw value → parsed value → description. **Click any parsed row, and the corresponding bytes in the input box are highlighted in reverse.**

Monitors smart ID card appointment quotas at the six Hong Kong Immigration Department registration offices, checking about every 2 minutes. When slots are released, it alerts subscribers via email / Feishu group. **A third-party public-interest tool, not an official Immigration Department service. ## Dashboard entry

- **Preferred (stable direct access from mainland China)**: https://hkid-quota-monitor.pages.dev/
- Backup: https://chen1111-a.github.io/hkid-quota-monitor/
  (github.io is intermittently unreachable from mainland networks. The jsDelivr/raw direct links carry a nosniff header and only display source code, so don't use them as web entry points.)

```
cron-job.org (every 2 minutes) ──▶ GitHub Actions
                            │  python -m quota_monitor.run
                            │  ├─ Fetch the Immigration Department's public quota API (read-only, one request at a time)
                            │  ├─ Diff against the previous-round snapshot → slot-release events
                            │  └─ commit data/ + refresh jsDelivr cache
                            ▼

# Femiwiki Infra

This is the Terraform code that defines the infrastructure of Femiwiki. The workspaces are `aws/`, `docker/`, `gcp/`, `github/`, `grafana/`, `healthchecks/`, and `mariadb/`. All of them run on [OpenTofu], and their state is stored in S3.

## Applying changes

Changes to any workspace are applied through a PR. Planning, approval, applying, and merging are handled by [terraform-github-tacos], and the flow of applying before merging is described in [Apply-before-merge] in that document. The Docker daemon in `docker/` is only open on the loopback interface of the edge box, so it is reached through an SSM tunnel. `mariadb/` connects to the MariaDB on the database host the same way. When you open a PR, `.github/workflows/tofu.yml` posts the plan as a comment. If the plan includes changes, the `<워크스페이스> apply` job in the same run waits for approval in the GitHub environment with that name. Approve it under Review deployments on the run page, and that plan gets applied. Image bump PRs follow the same flow. If you push a new commit, the pending approval of the previous run is cancelled, and the new run waits for approval again.

The result is written by [dflook/tofu-apply] on the status line at the bottom of the plan comment. 🟠 means applying is in progress, ✅ means applied, and ❌ means not applied or failed. Workflow run logs are deleted after some time, so once an apply finishes, each workspace leaves its apply log as a PR comment.

Merging comes next. The required check `tofu gate` only produces a result once the apply waiting for approval has finished, so a PR that has not been applied will not be merged. When the apply succeeds, the workflow merges the PR, so there is nothing else to do after applying.

Once an apply finishes for any workspace, the ```wikitext block in that PR's body is posted to [페미위키:업데이트] with the time the apply finished (to the minute) as its title, as is. gybeyond1/Veyra.body:
# Veyra

Veyra is a **short drama aggregator player**: an Android client (APK) + a self-hosted Node backend (Docker). It supports online playback of 红果 / 黄果 short dramas, private mode authentication, proxy bypass, and **download and merging on phone / NAS**.

> This project originated from [MrSsg/HuangguoAPP-for-Andriod](https://github.com/MrSsg/HuangguoAPP-for-Andriod) (GPL-3.0), but has independently evolved into the **Veyra** brand: an independent package name, independent backend image, and independent data directory. Content copyright belongs to the respective content sources; this project only provides the technical implementation. Do not use it for illegal purposes.

---

## Features

- **Multi-source playback**: Online playback of 红果 / 黄果 short dramas; the backend address is entered by the user on the login / registration page, **no private domain is built in**.
- **Account system**: Login / registration (registration toggle is dynamically controlled in the WebUI). Registration requires an admin dynamic code (OTP); accounts are not tied to devices.
- **Private mode**: Requires a backend dynamic code (OTP), authenticated once and tied to the account; admin accounts enter directly without an OTP.
- **Proxy bypass**: A proxy port can be configured in settings (effective only for 黄果). If the proxy is unreachable, traffic is automatically forwarded through the backend; 红果 is not affected.
- **Backend proxy**: The WebUI can configure the backend's outbound proxy (`http://ip:port`); when the backend fetches 黄果 resources, it goes through this proxy. proxy-test uses `google.com/generate_204` to check proxy connectivity.
- **Role permissions**: Regular users can only download to their phone; admins can download to NAS.
- **Download and merge**:
  - Phone: concurrent download (10 streams) → local normalization + merging into a single file; if merging fails, it automatically falls back to keeping individual episodes, and can be retried / re-merged.
  - NAS: the backend ffmpeg downloads, decrypts, and merges (avc3/hev1 + unified timebase); the output is directly playable.
  - The phone merge engine is a **self-developed NDK-ported ffmpeg + hand-written JNI** (C layer decryption / normalization / concat), aligned 1:1 in semantics with the backend downloader `server/downloader.js`.
- **WebUI admin console**: User list, role switching, deleting users, registration toggle, dynamic code display / reset, backend proxy configuration. Access requires the admin password (`ADMIN_PASSWORD`).

```
├── app/                      # Android client (Java + WebView UI)
│   └── src/main/
│       ├── java/com/veyra/gybeyond/   # main program (playback / download / merge / account / proxy / hot update)

Graphical interface for local Steam library installation and unlocking (Windows 10/11 · WinUI 3 · native compilation).

OSTGUI is the graphical interface for the [ZSteamTool](https://github.com/hazjy/ZSteamTool) kernel. The kernel injects into Steam and takes over ownership, depot decryption keys, and manifest requests. OSTGUI handles searching and adding games, generating Lua configs, managing added games, as well as online launch and launching without Steam deployment. This repository contains no kernel code and no game files.
## Features

- **Search & add**: Search by game name, AppID, or Steam link. Manifests come from MHub (requires an API Key), and keys and tokens come from Sudama. Optional: “Add all DLCs”, “Write fixed version config”, “Download Manifest”. The process can be cancelled.
- **Library management**: List / grid browsing and filtering, switching version mode, completing version configs, editing Lua, copying AppID and name, deleting.
- **Achievements**: Edit achievement unlock status. Changes are first written to a local backup, then saved manually with “Save to Steam” (requires Steam online).

- **Online**: Three routes: kernel-native, DLL injection (recommended), and AppID Changer.
- **Denuvo**: Import and export of authorization files (`.ost`). Export requires Steam to be online and the account to own the game.
- **Emulators**: Launch without Steam deployment (Steamless unpacking + Goldberg emulator) and without Ubisoft (experimental). Both support one-click restore.
- **Other**: Light / dark themes and Mica / Acrylic effects, running logs, check for updates, restart Steam.

- Windows 10 20H1 (19041) or later, x64

# lc-backend

## Service

1. An owner (`owner`) registers a campaign (`campaign`), and an admin (`admin`) creates first-come, first-served coupon flyers from LLM-generated templates, then pays to top up points.
2. Ad coupon feeds are served (`adserving`) to members (`member`), and when a member views a coupon, points are charged (`billing`) based on that impression.
3. When a first-come, first-served coupon event starts, members receive a coupon (`coupon`), and the owner at the store (`store`) scans the dynamic QR code in the coupon box to process the coupon redemption.

* Language: Java 21 (`eclipse-temurin:21.0.9`)
* Build: Gradle 8.14.3 (wrapper)
* Framework: Spring Boot 4.0.5
* Database: MySQL 8.4, Valkey 9.0

# QQ Agent Plus

A QQ group chat agent for Linux servers. It supports split-message replies, sending and receiving sticker packs, long-term memory, and built-in ops commands.

**Simplified Chinese** ｜ [English](https://github.com/sakurawwwxh/qq-agent-plus/blob/HEAD/README.en.md)

QQ Agent Plus is a QQ group chat agent for Linux servers. It connects to an external OneBot v11 protocol endpoint. Each trigger uses a separate OpenAI Chat Completions session. It does not depend on DSH, MCP, Electron, or Windows runtime environments.

## Features

The capabilities below all come from fixing real problems in live group chats. The failure mode and fix for each item are recorded in the [change list](https://github.com/sakurawwwxh/qq-agent-plus/blob/HEAD/docs/CHANGES.md).

- **Conversation behavior**: single-turn split-message replies, judging the mood of an image before responding, a sticker list kept in the system prompt (frequently used and unused stickers rotated, count adjustable), and a self-check before finishing.
- **Send pipeline**: network-layer send retries, QQ system emoji, message ID normalization, and fallback parsing of inline tool calls.
- **Sticker system**: automatically collects and prioritizes QQ favorite stickers, with lookup fallback and sync guardrails.
- **Games and reminders**: lightweight mini-games playable directly (word chain / number guessing / 20 Questions / Truth or Dare; dice rolls, lottery draws, and random roll-call use `dice` and the group member list). **Multiplayer games run by a state machine** (Number Bomb, Who Is the Undercover, Werewolf). Turns, vote counting, and rulings are handled by the system. Roles and night actions only go through private chat, so the model cannot leak them. These are experimental and off by default; Werewolf also requires checking it in the console allowlist. "X remind me to Y at time Z" is stored as a **persistent reminder** that survives restarts, and when it fires it is delivered in the agent's own voice.
- **Proactive speech**: three channels that can each be turned off (starting a topic when the chat is quiet, adding a follow-up when no one responds, and the model scheduling its own wake-ups), multiple active time windows, interval guardrails, skip-reason logs, and backfilling messages missed while offline after a restart.
- **Model access**: thinking levels translated per channel, configurable per provider and per task (Settings → Model API → "Advanced: Thinking Mode"), retry when a provider's moderation blocks a request, and fallback model switching.
- **Voice** (transcription and replies): voice messages, audio files, and video audio tracks are transcribed to text before being passed to the chat model. This works regardless of whether the model is multimodal.

shibing624/dual-mem.body:
## Why dual-mem You've told the AI three times, "I don't eat spicy food anymore," and it still recommends Sichuan restaurants. After dozens of rounds of chatting, it can recite every sentence you said, but it can't tell you your stable habits for getting things done. Coding conventions you laid out in Cursor, Codex doesn't know about. ### 1. 🏆 Same model, better recall, faster writes Extraction, answering, and scoring all use the same model (Qwen3.8-27B), the same embedding (bge-m3), and the same set of questions — **only the memory system is swapped**: | Memory system | LoCoMo
(308 questions) | LongMemEval
(24 questions) | PersonaMem-v2
(476 questions) | Single long-conversation write time
(seconds, lower is faster) | |---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | **dual-mem** | **74.7** | **91.7** | **50.0** | **503** | | hy-memory 2.0.4 | 66.6 | 70.8 | 43.5 | 2485 | | mem0 | 65.6 | 83.3 | 47.9 | 808 | **Ranks first on all three public benchmarks, with writes taking roughly one-fifth the time of hy-memory.** For the protocol, significance tests, question-type breakdown, and reproduction commands, see the [benchmark notes](https://github.com/shibing624/dual-mem/blob/main/docs/benchmarks.md). ### 2. 🧠 Two systems — that's the "dual" The "dual" in the name refers to the two memory systems in chat, and it is also the methodological layer to be described in the paper. - **System 1 (default `system1`)**: writes during the conversation. Verbatim quotes, facts, and personal profiles are stored in layers; when you change your mind, move to a new city, or update a plan, it appends a new version, keeps the history, and answers with the latest. - **dual / System 2 (`mode="dual"`, then call `digest()`)**: when a session wraps up, it synthesizes behavioral patterns and long-term profile (L3) across multiple pieces of evidence. Corresponding example: [`examples/02_dual.py`](https://github.com/shibing624/dual-mem/blob/main/examples/02_dual.py). ### 3. 🔗 Multiple agents, one memory MemHub connects the two systems above to multiple tools on your machine. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Hermes, and Agentica read and write the same memory, and data stays on your computer by default. ```bash pip install "dual-mem[all]" dual-mem hub install-service # runs in the background, starts on boot dual-mem hub install-host all #… ```

# yan-skills

Agent Skills for SEO and indie developers. **Building sites, choosing keywords, getting backlinks, checking data, and reviewing and iterating.** The whole pipeline is in this repo, and it's ready to run once installed.

By [Yan](https://github.com/yan-labs). Battle-tested for personal use and verified to work. Compatible with Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, and any platform that reads `SKILL.md`. MIT licensed, so use it freely.

```bash
npx skills add yan-labs/yan-skills -g --all
```

---

## What problem this solves

Someone running an independent site usually goes through a day like this:

In the morning, they want to start a new niche, so they first check whether the keyword has search volume and how hard it is to rank. The tool websites cost two hundred dollars a month, which is too expensive, so they open a dozen tabs and compare results by hand. At noon, they settle on a keyword and start building the site: scaffolding, Cloudflare, domain, GA, GSC. The full setup takes two days, and the next time they build a site, they go through it all again and hit the same pitfalls. In the afternoon, they need backlinks, so they dig up a shared list of “500 free backlink sites” and open the first twenty. Seventeen don't load, two require registration and review, and one asks you to place a link to them first. In the evening, they open GSC, see “Crawled – currently not indexed,” and don't know whether to change the content or submit again.

Three months later, on a different project, the whole process starts from scratch.

**This repo exists to end “starting from scratch.”** It turns each of these steps into scripts, data files, and decision rules that an AI agent can follow directly.
